q: How does CNOT infidelity in a noisy Qiskit Aer simulator (with T1/T2 + amplitude damping) scale with Scarani's selectivity ratio (omega_1 - omega_2)/omega_c, and does the paper's chosen '>= 4 omega_c' rule correspond to any particular infidelity threshold?
basis: Scarani derives selectivity inequalities in Section 2 that vanish entirely in an ideal statevector run; our DJ/Simon replication was noise-free, so the paper's core NMR-physics trade-off (selectivity vs. speed) was invisible to us.
next_steps: Build a parameterized 2-qubit NMR-Hamiltonian simulator in Qiskit Aer, sweep the (omega_1-omega_2)/omega_c ratio from 1.5 to 8, compile Scarani's CNOT as a selective sinc pulse of matched duration, and plot average CNOT infidelity vs. ratio; compare against the 2- and 4-omega_c thresholds Scarani asserts.

q: Scarani writes down QFT_n=2 as a full 4x4 DFT matrix (eq. 22) without ever counting gates or presenting the efficient Coppersmith circuit. How many one-qubit rotations + CNOTs does Qiskit's transpiler use to implement his eq. 21 for n = 2, 3, 4, 5 on all-to-all vs. linear-topology backends, and at what n does the survey's implicit 'one-liner' definition first mislead a reader about resource cost?
basis: We reproduced Scarani's eq. 22 matrix bit-identically, but neither the paper nor our replication counted gates; a survey aimed at undergraduates would benefit from an explicit gate-cost annotation.
next_steps: Transpile Qiskit's built-in QFT (both native and inverse) at n = 2..8 to the {H, CNOT, RZ} basis on both fully-connected and linear coupling maps; report gate counts + depth; identify the crossover where 'compute the DFT matrix then decompose' would exceed Coppersmith by more than 2x.

q: Scarani uses a physicist's clockwise-positive rotation convention where R_x(theta) has +i sin(theta) off-diagonals; Qiskit uses the opposite. Which of Scarani's four exercise circuits (3.1 GHZ, 3.2 NOT decomposition, 3.3 Bell readout, 3.4 QFT) require sign-flipping any single rotation angle to reproduce the paper's stated output state under Qiskit's convention, and does the paper's use of C^1_{2-} (CNOT flipping spin 1 when spin 2 is in |->) map to Qiskit's control-target convention without reordering?
basis: Our replication used the standard Qiskit basis (H + CNOT) as a shortcut rather than a literal port of Scarani's R_x(theta), R_y(theta), C^i_{j-} operators; a strict per-exercise reproduction would need a convention audit.
next_steps: Port Scarani's four exercises verbatim into Qiskit using QuantumCircuit.rx/ry/rz and explicit control-target orderings, compare statevectors to the paper's stated outputs (GHZ, |Phi+><Phi+| etc.), and record every sign or endianness fix required.

q: For Simon's algorithm with n = 3, what is the shallowest oracle depth that still implements a valid 2-to-1 f with hidden period s as a function of the Hamming weight |s|_H, and how does the required number of measurement rounds change if we deliberately use a non-minimum-depth 'randomized' oracle that adds spurious CNOT layers?
basis: Our Simon oracle used the textbook 'copy then controlled-XOR-with-s' construction and always recovered s in 2-4 rounds, but we never varied oracle depth or measured the algorithm's sensitivity to oracle design.
next_steps: Enumerate all valid depth-d Simon oracles for n=3 up to d = 6 by brute-forcing CNOT layer sequences and testing 2-to-1 + period property classically; then run each through the same simon_round() harness to correlate oracle depth with number of Simon rounds needed.

q: Scarani ends by explicitly punting quantum error correction as 'for specialists.' What fraction of the DJ (n=3) and Simon (n=3) circuits used in this replication would fail on a physical device at typical 2026-era single-/two-qubit gate infidelities (p1 ~ 1e-3, p2 ~ 5e-3), and at what n does DJ's 'one-query with probability 1' claim break down below 90% success without QEC?
basis: Our replication was noise-free and finished in under 3 seconds; the paper leaves a large instructive gap between 'it works in principle' and 'it works on a real device' precisely because it skips QEC.
next_steps: Rerun run_algorithms.py with Qiskit Aer's noise model built from IBM Falcon-era calibration (single-qubit ~1e-3, CNOT ~5e-3, T1/T2 ~ 100 microseconds); sweep n from 2 to 10 for DJ and n from 2 to 5 for Simon; plot success probability vs. n and compare to the noise-free (paper) prediction of unity.
